glossary.definition: Content inspection in and out across MCP, A2A, LLM and coding-agent traffic, for the attacks identity controls cannot see. In this lab: the lab's own deterministic stand-in. Ping release claim, UNVERIFIED on our tenant.

Four outcomes per policy: allow, alert, sanitize or block, with thresholds per category and overrides per key or per application. A threshold of 0 turns that outcome off. Ping release claim, UNVERIFIED on our tenant.
Redact the offending span and forward the rest of the content, instead of blocking all of it. Ping release claim, UNVERIFIED on our tenant.

Instructions that arrive in content the user never typed: a tool result, a retrieved document, a peer agent's message. The same words score higher than when typed by the user, because it is a channel the user never sees. Ping release claim, UNVERIFIED on our tenant.

The release goes from 5 kinds of personal data to 23, each numeric kind checksum-validated and selectable per kind (PIIKinds, console swagger name). The lab ships its OWN illustrative set of eleven, not Ping's list. Ping release claim, UNVERIFIED on our tenant.

glossary.term: Checksum validation and the near miss
glossary.definition: A numeric kind is only a finding if its checksum holds (Luhn, mod 97, mod 11, a weighted sum, a check letter). A card number with one digit wrong is a near miss and must not match. Each lab kind has a test for it.

Detectors for credentials by prefix, length, entropy floor and allowlist. The deck says 364 and 411 maintained rules (47 behavioural); the lab ships fifteen of its own, labelled lab examples. Ping release claim, UNVERIFIED on our tenant.

Rules paste in gitleaks rule format. One bad rule refuses the whole paste and the Errors list names each refused rule, one per line (imodelAIGuardRuleImport {Toml, Added, Errors}, console swagger names, 2026-10-31, schema only). Ping release claim, UNVERIFIED on our tenant.

A pasted regular expression is user-fed, so it is checked up front for nested quantifiers, backreferences, lookaround and huge repeat counts, and only ever runs in a worker thread with a hard time limit and an input cap.

A policy records what it would have caught without changing the outcome, so a rule can be authored, watched, and promoted to enforcement once the false-positive rate is known. In this lab a new rule starts in observe (lab-invented). Ping release claim, UNVERIFIED on our tenant.

glossary.term: Prompt logging, sealed to your key
glossary.definition: Prompts and responses retained under a public key you supply; only your private key opens them, entered in the console when you read a record; Privilege never holds it. Off until a tenant asks; nothing is recorded without a public key (modelPromptLogConfig, console swagger names). Ping release claim, UNVERIFIED on our tenant.
Ephemeral X25519 key agreement, HKDF-SHA256 and AES-256-GCM, in an envelope {v, kid, rid, epk, nonce, ct}. The envelope format is LAB-INVENTED: the product's format is not public.

A sealed record is decrypted in the console itself, at the moment you open it, with a private key you supply then. The lab generates the key pair in the browser with WebCrypto; the private half is never sent, never stored by default and never logged. Ping release claim, UNVERIFIED on our tenant.

Guard (every inspection result with the category, the corroborating rule, the direction, the decision and the agent and person behind it), Alerts (observation only) and Prompts (the sealed record list), filterable by agent, application, category, decision, flow and event. Ping release claim, UNVERIFIED on our tenant.
Each finding cross-referenced to OWASP LLM Top 10, the OWASP Agentic Top 10, MITRE ATLAS and NIST AI RMF labels. In this lab the labels are lab-illustrative, not Ping's versioned catalogue.

glossary.term: OWASP Agentic AI Top 10 (ASI01 to ASI10)
glossary.definition: Each category maps to a named control, with the deck's own gaps stated: ASI04 fingerprint pinning pending, ASI06 memory-write inspection shipped with gateway integration in progress, and notes on ASI08, ASI09 and ASI10. Ping release claim, UNVERIFIED on our tenant.

sources.use: Field names for PIIKinds, the category thresholds, the custom rule, the rule import and the prompt-log settings. It proves names exist, not behaviour.

cards.label: Action 1: An ordinary request
cards.description: Nothing sensitive. No rule fires, the content goes through, and the inspection still appears in Agent Insights with the person and the agent behind it.

cards.label: Action 2: Contact details in a prompt
cards.description: An e-mail address and a telephone number are personal data, but low risk by default: the score reaches the alert threshold and not the sanitize one. The prompt goes through and the alert is recorded.

cards.label: Action 3: A card number and an identifier
cards.description: Both numbers pass their checksum, so both are real findings. The policy says sanitize: each offending span is redacted and the rest of the prompt is forwarded. A number that fails its checksum would not have fired.

cards.label: Action 4: An instruction override typed by the user
cards.description: A direct injection scores 0.75: above the sanitize threshold, below block. The offending phrase is redacted and the rest forwarded. Compare the next action, where the very same words arrive from somewhere else.

cards.label: Action 5: Hidden instructions in a tool result
cards.description: The words are the same family as the last action, but this content came back from a tool: a channel the user never typed and never saw. It scores higher (indirect injection), and the hidden comment fires a second rule. The result is withheld.

cards.label: Action 6: A credential in a prompt
cards.description: The credential matches a secret detector (a prefix, a length and an entropy floor). Secrets are blocked outright by default, so it never reaches the model. This one is the labelled mock credential; anything real you type in Live is masked everywhere.

cards.label: Action 7: A model output that smuggles data in an image link
cards.description: Inspection runs on the way out as well as in. A markdown image whose address carries a query string is a classic way to leak data when the page renders it. Blocked on output.

cards.label: Paste your own rules
cards.description: One bad rule refuses the whole paste; a hostile pattern is refused before it can run.

cards.label: Seal a prompt to your own key
cards.description: Make a key in the browser, record a prompt sealed to it, open it with the private key; try the wrong key.

cards.label: Ask what happened
cards.description: Guard, Alerts and Prompts with filters over a live view or a window of 24 hours to 30 days.

cards.label: The OWASP Agentic Top 10, as qualified
cards.description: The deck's own gaps repeated exactly, never rounded up to full coverage.

cards.label: Why it matters: AIGuard (slide 53)
cards.description: Challenge: authorization cannot see content, so an agent following hidden instructions in a retrieved document can exfiltrate data entirely within policy; this blind spot is what security review flags on every agent rollout. Technical: content is inspected in and out on MCP, A2A, LLM and coding-agent traffic, and deterministic rules add no availability dependency. Business: a fraction of the cost of one incident, and framework-mapped evidence for AI governance sign-off. Ping claims, unverified on our tenant.

cards.label: Why it matters: Agent Insights (slide 54)
cards.description: Challenge: enforcement is only half of an investigation; decisions and detections scatter across surfaces, so what happened takes days to answer and incidents stay open. Technical: one record set across every gateway surface, with sealed prompt content and clear-text searchable metadata. Business: incidents close faster, and assessor requests leave in the shape they were asked for, which means less investigation effort and shorter audits. Ping claims, unverified on our tenant.

cards.label: Why it matters: Prompt Logging (slide 50)
cards.description: Challenge: prompts and responses are exactly the content an investigation needs and exactly the content a vendor should not be able to read, so teams refuse retention that hands the vendor the content and investigations stall. Technical: content sealed to your public key and decrypted only in your console session, with Privilege never holding the private half. Business: full forensic retention becomes acceptable to security and legal, and investigations get the record without a data-trust concession. Ping claims, unverified on our tenant.

cards.label: Why it matters: OWASP Agentic AI Top 10 (slide 55)
cards.description: Challenge: security review now demands precise answers against the OWASP ASI taxonomy, and vague coverage claims stall approval and procurement. Technical: each ASI category maps to a named control and mechanism, with the ASI08, ASI09 and ASI10 coverage notes stated plainly. Business: framework-mapped answers accelerate security approval and de-risk the purchase. Ping claims, unverified on our tenant.

cards.label: Diagrams
cards.description: Two diagrams: content inspected in and out with a graduated answer; and prompts sealed to your key.

cards.description: Preflight checks and the demo-health/1 endpoint.
